s320_prevention_capability.description: Assess whether current Gate -1 implementation would have prevented the S320 wrong-variant remediation failure.
s320_prevention_capability.s320_context: S320 executed a DL-026 remediation script targeting Unprocessed canonical seeds in Pack C/D. QID-only targeting matched rotation-group variants instead of canonical seeds. Result: 0 correct fills, both packs restored from backups, zero certification progress.

prevention_assessment.operational_prevention: Steps 1-3 prevent wrong-pack targeting and blank-CC items from entering remediation. These alone would NOT have prevented S320 because the S320 items had valid QID formats, valid CC, and correct pack attribution. Steps 4-5 (TemplateFamily + compound key) are required to distinguish canonical seeds from rotation variants.
prevention_assessment.governance_prevention: Rules 9-10 (FM-001 through FM-008 forbidden methodologies) would have blocked QID-only targeting regardless of Gate -1 implementation status. Any S320-class remediation script must use compound-key targeting — this is HARD_BLOCK enforced.
prevention_assessment.full_prevention_when: When steps 4-5 are deployed (S206/S207), S320-class failures are architecturally impossible. Until then, Rules 9-10 provide a governance-layer prevention that blocks QID-only targeting scripts.

s320_prevention_capability.confidence: HIGH — the governance layer (Rules 9-10) is sufficient to block S320-class scripts. The identity layer (steps 4-5) provides machine-enforced prevention on top of governance enforcement.
